events.title: Teatro Olimpico Opens in Vicenza
events.description: The Teatro Olimpico in Vicenza, Italy, was inaugurated. It was designed by the Renaissance architect Andrea Palladio and is one of the oldest surviving indoor theatres in the world.
events.significance: Its elaborate permanent stage set, with forced-perspective streets, influenced theatre design for generations.

events.title: Florida Becomes the 27th U.S. State
events.description: Florida was admitted to the Union as the 27th state. It joined as a slave state, and Iowa was admitted as a free state the following year.
events.significance: Its admission was part of the territorial expansion and the slavery-balance politics that led up to the American Civil War.

events.title: Alexander Graham Bell Is Born
events.description: Alexander Graham Bell was born in Edinburgh, Scotland. He became a teacher of the deaf and an inventor, and he later moved to North America.
events.significance: Bell is credited with inventing the telephone, which changed how people communicate around the world.

events.title: Tsar Alexander II Issues the Emancipation Manifesto
events.description: Tsar Alexander II signed the Emancipation Manifesto, which abolished serfdom across the Russian Empire. The date is March 3 on the modern calendar, and it was February 19 on the old Russian calendar. The reform freed millions of peasants from bondage to landowners.
events.significance: It was one of the most sweeping social reforms in Russian history and reshaped the country's society and economy.

events.title: Rodney King Beating Is Filmed in Los Angeles
events.description: Los Angeles police officers severely beat motorist Rodney King, and a bystander recorded it on video. When the footage was broadcast, it caused a global outcry.
events.significance: The acquittal of the officers a year later set off the 1992 Los Angeles riots, and the case prompted a national debate on police brutality and race.
